newsitem.title: GERMANY: German swine fever outbreak neutral for feeds.
newsitem.headline: German swine fever outbreak neutral for feeds.

text.p: The latest outbreak of swine fever in Germany has not been felt in the feeds sector, said Hubert Grote, managing director of feeds industry association FFMI.
"The number of affected and slaughtered animals is relatively low," he said.
Germany on Monday unilaterally banned exports from four states and authorities have ordered the slaughter of more than 14,000 pigs to contain the disease.
This compared with 24.12 million live pigs at the last count on December 3, 1996, which was 1.6 percent more than a year earlier.
European Union veterinary authorities want a ban on the export of pigs from five states and two districts in a sixth.
The Netherlands on Thursday also ordered the destruction of between 20,000 and 30,000 pigs after two local outbreaks.
Germany had just freed itself of the disease in 1996 after recurring problems in the early 1990s led to the preventive slaughter of up to one million animals.
"We had just been noticing growth rates in pigfeed sales over the last few months, as markets were returning to normal," Grote said.
Compound feed for pigs may include between 10 and 40 percent of feed grain, soymeal and other protein sources as well as corngluten, molasses and a variety of other feeds.
